story.title: Ohm's law in series and in parallel

scenes.heading: One cell, three resistors
sentences: A cell can push current through resistors in two ways.
How much current flows in each?

scenes.heading: In series
sentences: A 12.0 volt cell drives one current through three resistors in a row.
The current is 0.200 amperes, the same in every resistor.
The voltages across them are 2.00, 4.00 and 6.00 volts, and they add up to the cell.

scenes.heading: In parallel
sentences: Now the same three resistors side by side across the 12.0 volt cell.
The currents are 1.20, 0.600 and 0.400 amperes, and they add up to 2.20 amperes from the cell.

scenes.heading: Same rule, different shape
sentences: Ohm's law holds for every resistor.
In series the current is shared, and in parallel the voltage is.
